scope.invariant: A package accepted by native verification is an owned bounded snapshot with unambiguous allowed paths/resources, exact integrity and correctly scoped signature evidence, independent of installation authority.
scope.selectedChain: verify(owned Vec<u8>) -> bounded ZIP framing -> normalized resource paths -> metered decompression -> exact integrity/signature/manifest/resource checks -> private VerifiedPackage -> direct native stage/verify_pair and PreviewSession snapshot consumption.

declaredStatus.claim: S14 implemented: bounded owned ZIP/resources, original-byte signatures and remote sourcemap rejection; application installation/recovery remains a distinct authority chain.

checks.question: Does one framework-independent owner validate bytes without filesystem, transport, grant or execution authority?
checks.detail: Normal dependency tree contains protocol, bounded ZIP/DEFLATE, SHA-256, Ed25519 and Unicode support; no Tauri/runtime/account/HTTP/SQLite dependency. Read is used over an owned in-memory Cursor. This is the verifier boundary, not an installation-authority audit.

checks.question: Do framing, paths, resource restrictions, budgets and cooperative cancellation reject forbidden inputs?
checks.detail: Framing checks count/size before ZIP construction; paths reject traversal, devices and normalized collisions; decompression meters actual output. Existing corpus covers representative archive/path/bomb refusals. Additional oversize archive and mid-read cancellation assertions pass. However, remote sourceMappingURL directives with a matching suffix in query/fragment are accepted (B16-P01). This does not certify every resource format or race.

checks.question: Are exact payload integrity, original-byte signatures and the owned immutable loading snapshot preserved?
checks.detail: VerifiedPackage fields are private and expose borrowed immutable values. Integrity covers all payloads and excludes only integrity/signature metadata, rejects duplicates and compares actual size/hash. verify_strict signs domain plus original directory bytes. stage retains verified owned bytes; verify_pair validates private code and returns that same snapshot as bytes, without reopening it after verification. PreviewSession holds the VerifiedPackage and derives Candidate from its manifest/hash/signer. Persistence, transactions, migration and GC are not certified by these excerpts.

checks.question: Does signature validation remain distinct from publisher trust and native authorization?
checks.detail: signer() explicitly reports possession only; unsigned packages remain valid inputs, not approved installations. Revocation verification requires caller-injected trusted fingerprints and time, rejects untrusted/expired/future/tampered lists, and can accept independently provisioned roots. No package key is automatically promoted to a distribution root. Actual app root provisioning and persisted revocation union are deferred to B16-revocations-recovery; preview/consent/target admission internals are outside this subbatch.

checks.question: Do owned tests substantiate the documented validation claims and the newly checked failure paths?
checks.detail: Three existing Rust integration tests pass, including 43 shared package cases and public Node signature vectors; Node validates the same 43 cases and an ephemeral Rust signature. Scoped Clippy passes. The remote-map corpus case does not cover query/fragment suffix masking: two added negative probes reproduce the missing refusal in both implementations. Permanent corpus changes and implementation repair remain a separate task.

findings.title: Remote sourcemaps bypass rejection through a matching query or fragment suffix
findings.trigger: Seal an otherwise valid sandbox-code package whose dist/main.js ends with //# sourceMappingURL=https://example.invalid/main.js.map?sourceMappingURL=main.js.map (or the equivalent #sourceMappingURL=main.js.map fragment). Keep a valid local dist/main.js.map and recompute integrity.
findings.effect: The check compares the entire comment line suffix instead of the complete directive URL. Both validators return a verified package containing a forbidden remote sourcemap reference, contrary to the S14 resource contract. This audit demonstrates admission of the forbidden directive only; it does not claim the VM or WebView fetched a remote map or bypassed execution/network authority.

reproduction.prerequisites: From repository root, cargo build -p am-plugin-package --locked --message-format=json > .codex-tmp/audit-b16-package-verification/build.jsonl. Ignored probe source and fixture files remain local.
reproduction.expected: Only local main.js.map accepted; all remote directive URLs return Resource.
reproduction.actual: Both query-mask and fragment-mask variants accepted by Rust and Node; diagnostic command exits 1.

findings.suggestedNextAction: Parse the actual sourceMappingURL directive value and require its complete value to be the exact allowed local reference. Apply the same rule in Rust and Node and add both negative variants to the SDK-owned raw package corpus, with local-map positives retained. Do not merely add another forbidden substring test.
